feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback strengthens the value of molecule-specific loading contrasts. m51 and m99 showed substantial onset differences across amounts at 10/1, while completion changed much less; m83 showed a smaller 10/1 contrast than its 20/1 contrast, supporting ratio-dependent loading effects. m182 measurements supported a completion-specific amount association at 1/1 and 2/1. The m108 and m122 results showed that related ethers can have different endpoint responses, and m124 did not support the proposed early maximum. m79 and m77 both contradicted earlier predicted decreases, but m77 retained an unusual short measured interval that merits bracketing. m158 and m48 rejected their predicted late completion growth or decline. These outcomes shift the batch toward earlier baselines, matched amount contrasts, and local curvature measurements, while avoiding further redundant sampling of already anchored benzoate segments.
batch_rationale: The batch combines failure repair with chemically meaningful local experiments. It measures m51, m99, m135, m67 and m97 to improve loading-transfer learning across alcohol and ester environments; m182 and m8 target completion-specific loading effects; m77 and m76 audit whether an unusual alpha-bromoester response transfers across related structures. m98, m10, m3 and m158 constrain unsupported local extrema and endpoint coupling. The m43, m34 and m35 measurements expand solvent-response coverage for halogenated aromatic ketones, while m18 covers a long-chain ester regime. The selected tuples are distinct and span strong, intermediate and weak eluents, multiple loading amounts, and several structural environments. These labels can improve Row-distribution generalization by repairing baselines, locating response knees, learning endpoint-specific curvature, and reducing unjustified transfer of sparse curves. Loading amount remains associated with recorded V and therefore tests catalog-condition associations rather than an isolated causal mass effect. V2 minus V1 is treated as elution interval width; prediction intervals and CW distance are auxiliary model-behavior and coverage signals.
